howItWasMadeImpossible: No credential is reachable: the scratch profile has no credentials.index.json, and KeychainStore.get returns null without spawning `security` when the index does not list the account (credential-store.ts:209). OPENROUTER_API_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY and four others are scrubbed from the child environment.

The launcher is bypassed. ~/.rune/bin/rune ends in `exec rune-compiled "$@"` but first does `source "$HOME/.rune/.env"` - hard-coded to $HOME, not RUNE_HOME - which would have loaded the founder's two live keys into the child. The driver runs rune-compiled directly with RUNE_TOOLS_BIN set exactly as the launcher sets it; the only other launcher behaviour skipped is the build-freshness warning, which would have printed into the captured frames.
The only provider is local: the seed sets [llm] defaultProvider = "ollama", the one preset marked `local`, registered with no key at base URL localhost:11434 (provider-registry.ts:141).

No text was ever submitted. The only bytes written to the pty are /config, /help, /model, /quit, arrow-down, Enter inside a picker, the digits 1 and 2 inside a picker, and Escape. Every digit press is gated behind a wait_for on the sub-picker's own footnote, because a digit typed in composer mode would sit in the composer and the next Enter would submit it. And when the / palette has matches, Enter picks a palette entry and cannot submit free text (tui.ts:inputKey).
No network at all: [update] check = false was seeded, and refreshUpdateCheck is the only host this build contacts at startup (upgrade-cli.ts:216).

behaviorChanges.change: Headless exit codes for unfinished runs
behaviorChanges.impact: A run that was cancelled, halted by the supervisor, or hit a turn or output-token ceiling now reports ok:false and exits non-zero, carrying a stopReason in the --json/--stream-json envelope. It previously exited 0 with whatever partial text it had, which a benchmark harness scores as a pass. Partial output is still preserved. This is the change most likely to surprise an existing script.

behaviorChanges.change: A check only closes the step it speaks to
behaviorChanges.impact: A passing command that does not correspond to the open step's touched files no longer closes that step: it still counts as a run, stays on the record and in the Decision Record, and the refusal says "no passing check", never "nothing ran". The rule STANDS DOWN for a step that touched no files, because there is nothing to relate to — that is the residual, and it is deliberate.

behaviorChanges.change: Read-only toolchain binds on Linux, on by default
behaviorChanges.impact: 16 named home-relative toolchain directories are now readable inside the Linux sandbox. This is a real widening of the read surface, chosen over leaving cargo/bun broken inside the sandbox — which historically ends with users turning the sandbox off. $HOME itself is never bound and no credential store is inside any of them.

behaviorChanges.change: An explicit RUNE_TOOLS_BIN/RUNE_TOOLS_BINARY wins over target/
behaviorChanges.impact: Test binary selection is now explicit and a wrong path throws instead of skipping. THE TRAP: running these suites from inside a Rune session means the launcher's own RUNE_TOOLS_BIN=~/.rune/bin/rune-tools is exported, so they grade the INSTALLED binary rather than a freshly built one. Loud, but surprising.

behaviorChanges.change: The network opt-in emits a user-visible notice
behaviorChanges.impact: Starting a host- or port-restricted plugin under allowUnsandboxedTools on a backend that cannot filter endpoints now returns a notice the Engine drains into MCP notices, instead of a line in a log. startPluginTools().notices changes shape.

behaviorChanges.change: The inline-check classifier reads code, not text
behaviorChanges.impact: Nine shapes that previously classified as executed checks — a printed assertion word, an assertion word in a variable or a -p literal, words inside comments, a verdict swallowed by a bare catch — are now execution receipts. They earn a citable receipt and no verdict. Every remaining limit of the classifier errs toward demotion, never toward a false check; it still cannot prove an assertion actually executed.
